title: The founding questions
premise: The model specified obligations precisely and witnessed their breach almost nowhere. Requirements, verifications, exceptions, and communication policies were all stated with real precision, and in each case the execution-side counterpart that would catch a violation was missing. Loop 1 asks each of the twelve named roles what it actually needs to know, and invents the atomic predicates required to answer.
name: Loop 1: The founding questions

title: Questions only loop 1 made askable
premise: Loop 1 established WHAT can go wrong: a blocking control unmet, a verification skipped, a send refused, a claim whose source has left. Loop 2 asks the questions that only exist once those columns do — about the QUALITY of the assurance rather than its presence. Three examples that had no expressible form before loop 1 ran: only 4 of 13 requirements have any computed witness at all, so which controls are still trusted purely on assertion; verification_outcomes.is_self_witnessed reads 3/4, so how much of the evidence is the executor vouching for themselves; and send_intents.is_silently_dropped reads 4/7, a failure mode that could not be named until IsClearedToSend existed to refuse a send in the first place. Every loop-2 question records, in its own provenance, the loop-1 predicates that made it possible.
name: Loop 2: Questions only loop 1 made askable

title: Loop 3: the three gaps the source articles named and the model didn't have
premise: Comparing this rulebook against the four "Intentional Arrangement" Process Knowledge Management articles surfaced three concepts the essays argue for at length that had no table: process mining as an elicitation channel, controlled vocabulary/taxonomy, and the informal knowledge-broker network. Unlike loops 1-2, this loop is not a full 12-role sweep — it is exactly these three named gaps, each owned by the role that would actually ask the question.
name: Loop 3: Loop 3: the three gaps the source articles named and the model didn't have

title: Structure the executions cannot show
premise: Every witness in loops 1-3 reads either a single row or a single edge: whether this transition was traversed, whether this control was satisfied. The step graph itself is cyclic (Fallback and Alternative transitions send work back to earlier steps), and questions about its shape (which steps can be re-entered, which controls must hold on every pass) are reachability over paths of any length. Transitive closure is provably not expressible in first-order logic with aggregates, so no formula answers them. Loop 4 adds the closure of StepTransitions as a substrate-native closure field and asks the questions only it makes askable.
name: Loop 4: Structure the executions cannot show
